findings.source_passage: The adjective 'old' was misleading. Their united ages would certainly not have totalled forty-five.
findings.source_locator: Opening paragraph, after the greeting exchange
findings.why_it_matters: This is a crisp, ironic narratorial aside that establishes Christie's light-touch omniscient voice in its first appearance; its absence removes the first instance of the narrator's dry wit.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two-sentence aside verbatim immediately after the greeting exchange, before the 'Not seen you' line.

findings.source_passage: His face was pleasantly ugly--nondescript, yet unmistakably the face of a gentleman and a sportsman.
findings.source_locator: Physical description of Tommy, after seating at Lyons'
findings.why_it_matters: This oxymoronic phrase 'pleasantly ugly' is a signature character-establishing line; the draft retains only the red hair and the suit, stripping the characterisation that defines Tommy for the whole novel.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'pleasantly ugly—nondescript, yet unmistakably the face of a gentleman and a sportsman' phrasing within the Tommy description block.

findings.source_passage: there was character and charm in the elfin lines of her little face, with its determined chin and large, wide-apart grey eyes that looked mistily out from under straight, black brows.
findings.source_locator: Physical description of Tuppence, same paragraph as Tommy's
findings.why_it_matters: The source gives a precise, memorable physical portrait that anchors Tuppence's character visually; the draft collapses this to 'elfin-faced,' losing the determined chin and the distinctive grey-eyed description that critics and readers return to.
findings.suggested_fix: Expand the Tuppence description to include the determined chin, wide-apart grey eyes under straight black brows—this is the novel's definitive portrait of her.

findings.source_passage: a joint venture! It struck me as such a romantic phrase to come across in the middle of musty old figures. It's got an Elizabethan flavour about it--makes one think of galleons and doubloons.
findings.source_locator: Tuppence explaining the 'joint venture' phrase, before naming the company
findings.why_it_matters: This is the voice-defining passage that gives thematic colour to the whole enterprise; the Elizabethan/galleons digression explains why two broke young people romanticise their predicament and is the tonal heart of the chapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Tuppence's riff on 'joint venture'—the Elizabethan flavour, galleons, and doubloons—before the company name is announced.

findings.source_passage: It's not half so insane as a thing I read this morning beginning 'Petunia' and signed 'Best Boy.'
findings.source_locator: After Tommy says the ad reads like a hoax or a lunatic wrote it
findings.why_it_matters: This period-specific comic detail (lonely-hearts column argot) is a register-establishing period marker and a sharp comic beat; its removal flattens the exchange to bare plot mechanics.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-insert the 'Petunia'/'Best Boy' line as Tuppence's riposte to Tommy's 'lunatic' remark.

findings.source_passage: catching odds and ends of conversation as they did so. 'And--do you know, she sat down and _cried_ when I told her she couldn't have the flat after all.'
findings.source_locator: Wandering for a table at Lyons', before Jane Finn mention
findings.why_it_matters: The overheard snatches of conversation create a period-realist texture and contrast with Tommy's Jane Finn snippet; excising them weakens the naturalness of that coincidental detail.
findings.suggested_fix: A single overheard line before Tommy's Jane Finn remark would restore the ambient texture; not strictly required but improves period voice.

findings.source_passage: Tommy was holding the paper thoughtfully. His face burned a deeper red.
findings.source_locator: After Tuppence tears out the leaf and hands the ad to Tommy
findings.why_it_matters: This small physical beat—Tommy's blush—signals genuine vulnerability beneath the banter and is the emotional hinge before his 'shall we really?' question; losing it flattens the moment.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the detail of Tommy holding the paper and his face flushing before his 'Shall we really try it?' line.

summary: The draft preserves plot and dialogue adequately but erases four medium-severity voice and characterisation passages—the opening narratorial aside, Tommy's 'pleasantly ugly' description, Tuppence's galleons-and-doubloons digression, and the 'Petunia'/'Best Boy' comic beat—triggering the regenerate threshold.
